questions.corrige_markdown:
Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a function of $x$. By the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy) = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, and by the chain rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(y^2) = 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$$6x - 4\left(y + x\frac{dy}{dx}\right) + 4y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0.$$

$$6x - 4y - 4x\frac{dy}{dx} + 4y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0.$$

Collect the terms in $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$$(4y - 4x)\frac{dy}{dx} = 4y - 6x \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{4y - 6x}{4y - 4x} = \frac{2y - 3x}{2y - 2x}.$$

Multiplying numerator and denominator by $-1$:

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3x - 2y}{2x - 2y}. \qquad\blacksquare$$

(valid where $x \neq y$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{x + 10}{x^2 - x - 12}$, express $f(x)$ in partial fractions.

Hence, show that $\displaystyle\int_5^7 f(x)\,dx = \ln\left(\frac{36}{5}\right)$. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Partial fractions.** Factorise the denominator: $x^2 - x - 12 = (x - 4)(x + 3)$. The degree of the numerator ($1$) is less than that of the denominator ($2$), so

$$\frac{x + 10}{(x-4)(x+3)} = \frac{A}{x - 4} + \frac{B}{x + 3} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x + 10 = A(x + 3) + B(x - 4).$$

Put $x = 4$: $14 = 7A$, so $A = 2$. Put $x = -3$: $7 = -7B$, so $B = -1$.

$$\boxed{f(x) = \frac{2}{x - 4} - \frac{1}{x + 3}}$$

Check at $x = 5$: $f(5) = \dfrac{15}{8}$ and $\dfrac{2}{1} - \dfrac18 = \dfrac{15}{8}$. Correct.

**The integral.** On $[5, 7]$ we have $x - 4 > 0$ and $x + 3 > 0$, so the logarithms need no modulus signs:

$$\int_5^7 f(x)\,dx = \Bigl[\,2\ln(x - 4) - \ln(x + 3)\,\Bigr]_5^7 = \bigl(2\ln 3 - \ln 10\bigr) - \bigl(2\ln 1 - \ln 8\bigr).$$

Since $\ln 1 = 0$:

$$= 2\ln 3 - \ln 10 + \ln 8 = \ln 9 + \ln 8 - \ln 10 = \ln\frac{9 \times 8}{10} = \ln\frac{72}{10} = \ln\frac{36}{5}. \qquad\blacksquare$$

Numerical check: $\ln(36/5) = \ln 7.2 = 1.9741$, and $2\ln 3 - \ln 10 + \ln 8 = 2.1972 - 2.3026 + 2.0794 = 1.9741$.
